1.explanation:
• lighthouse-cli/run.js is the CLI entry point that catches all runtime errors and directly prints err.message (the raw ICU key) instead of invoking the i18n formatter.  
• lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js defines the LHEError class and holds the ICU message templates, but its constructor never calls the i18n layer to swap the template key for a localized string.  
• lighthouse-cli/printer.js is responsible for formatting CLI output; it should be updated to ensure that any error it prints (including fatal errors) is passed through the i18n formatter before going to stderr.
1.bug_scenario:
When you invoke the Lighthouse CLI with a URL that can’t be loaded (for example “not-a-valid-url”), the run.js script enters its fatal-error catch block and prints the raw ICU template identifier instead of a translated message. In the screenshot you can see:  

  Runtime error encountered: lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js | urlInvalid # 0  
  LHEError: INVALID_URL

This means the LHEError’s ICU key ("urlInvalid") was never looked up in the locale files before being written to stderr.

2.explanation:
• lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js is where LHEError is defined along with its ICU template key and friendlyMessage getter. On errors it holds both the template identifier and arguments used for i18n lookup.
• lighthouse-cli/run.js is the entry point for CLI execution. It invokes the core runner, catches any thrown LHEError on a fatal path, and passes it along for printing – but it never triggers the i18n lookup before handing off the error.
• lighthouse-cli/printer.js implements writeFatalError (and related routines) that format and dump the error to stderr. In the current code it prints err.message or raw err.code/template instead of using err.friendlyMessage (i.e. calling i18n.getFormatted). As a result the ICU identifier is shown instead of a localized string. To fix the bug, the run/printer code needs to import and swap to the correct locale at startup (via i18n.swapLocale) and then use err.friendlyMessage when printing fatal errors.
2.bug_scenario: When you invoke the Lighthouse CLI with a URL that causes a fatal runtime error (for example “not-a-valid-url”), the CLI’s error handler prints the raw ICU template identifier and code (e.g. “lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js | urlInvalid # 0”) instead of looking up and printing the human‐friendly, localized message. In other words, the i18n lookup never happens on the fatal‐error path, so users see the un-translated template key rather than a readable error.
